The home of “Anne of Green Gables” is across the field and the largest golf course in the world. 5 miles long.

cards.inscription: Monday - Dear Folks, Here we are back in the good old Island. We are staying at Cavendish Beach. The water is lovely and warm. Today was sunny. You would all like it here. The food is good and we are taking things easy. Hope you are all fine and fit. Will see you soon. Love Keith & Jean

cards.inscription: Dear Katherine, This is the home of one of my girlhood friends - yours no doubt too. Remember Anne? I want to thank you for helping us out with the nice package for the Parcel Post sale. We cleared about $22.00 on the affair! My cousin got your package and had lots of fun with it. She was tickled pink and is still showing it around. Thanks again.

cards.inscription: Charlottetown PEI 9-9-1930 Dear Chas, Thought you might like a card from here. Drove as far as roads come on the mainland and over here on train ferry last night. Am now 600 miles east of NYC & 400 east of Boston. This is the capital of the Island also largest city. Population 14,000.

Although unknown to each other personally we ?? know each other.

cards.inscription: I received your postal and was very glad to hear that you arent getting married. I won’t be home in Easter but expect to be home in June for good. Hope to hear more from you soon.

cards.inscription: Many thanks for Christmas wishes. Aunt Edith is here. So sorry not to see you in the fall but hope to be here for the reunion in the summer. All join me in best wishes for a Happy New Year for the gang.

cards.inscription: Dear Mrs. M. Just a line from PEI. Are having a splendid time. Hope you are well and most through serving. Had a letter from B yesterday. The boys are having a regular time.

cards.inscription: Cherry Valley RR No 1, P.E.I. Dear Mr Mac Alliston: Received your two pretty cards quite awhile ago pardon for long delay. I wa away at arrival of cards but here goes a card to Auburn, Ont. So you are making maple syrup. When you write, tell me all about how you make it as I never have seen it made? I live on a farm too, of about 100 acres with my mother, three sisters and little bro’. My father died 13 years ago, my eldest brother went away when he was 18, he is away 9 years now.

cards.inscription: Brackley Beach Aug 23 It is lovely here this morning. Clear and cool. I have enjoyed the places very much and am feeling much better. We are leaving next Wednesday and expect to reach Boston August 31. I hope you have ?? happy swimming.

cards.title: New Canadian National Railway Hotel at Charlottetown, P.E. Island.

cards.inscription: Dear Muriel, Just a card to say hello. Having a grand time.

cards.inscription: 9 - 6 - 09 On Steamer Trinidad at Charlottetown.Fine voyage from Picton. Rough sea but easy riding. The three jolly tars were not so jolly between Boston and Halifax. Am having a great time.

cards.inscription: Dear Mrs Black, We are right near High Park and I go there to swim. My school right in the block we live in. I hope your pictures are good.

cards.title: Rocky Point, P.E.I.
cards.inscription: Will get to Boston between 8 and 9 o’clock Sunday morning. Don’t get in before nine.

cards.title: Clinton, P.E. Island.
cards.inscription: Dear Mrs. Land - We are having a very nice holiday. We had a card from Lois & Lily not long ago. Kind regards to all.

cards.inscription: Was sorry that I could not be with Charlie yesterday. Ina was at her home in Vince, will be glad to take in that trip as soon as she returns.

cards.title: Prince of Wales College, Charlottetown, P.E. Island
cards.inscription: Dear Barbara, This is the college where my sister Marion graduated from, she just got home last Saturday. We have been on PEI a week now and we’re staying two more. Having a grand time, we picked wild strawberries this morning and aren’t they good.

cards.title: Soldiers’ Monument, Charlottetown, P.E.I.
cards.inscription: Aug 24, 1914. Dear Florence, Just a line to let you know I have reached this town safely. Have had a delightful trip. This is a pretty little town. We have a day here and a day in Sidney tomorrow. I think reach St Johns Friday morning.

cards.title: Kildare Capes, P.E. Island.
cards.inscription: Hello Ma, Yes sir, I am actually in PEI and is it nice! ALl I need is a car tho to make it perfect plus a few friends…

cards.inscription: Dear Ed, I know this market would interest you. The women bring in their products, butter, berries, vegetables, eggs, etc. and sell them at very reasonable prices. It reminds me of a big fair. People here are 50 years back. Farming is excellent. Farmers prosperous. Very few Fords. We are on the north short today and the water is as warm as Buzzard’s Bay. Harry is going to write you. We are going along the Gulf of St Lawrences to the Bay of Chaleur. Florence.

The boat in picture was to have come over today from Nova Scotia and I hoped to have caught it back tomorrow. Love from Owen.

cards.inscription: Summerside P.E.I. Aug 13th 1906 Dear Miss Dobbie, This is our first stop since Montreal which we left on Friday AM. We had an elegant time till we got out in the Gulf Saturday night and then we did not care where we were. I spent Sunday in bed but feel all right today. A.H.B. was very brave and stayed on deck but gave in before we landed. We have most of the day on shore and tomorrow will be in Charlottetown but there is nothing to see. It is a good thing A.D. is not on this boat because I am sure he could not get into the bunks at all they are so small. Hope you had a good time anyway and are getting fat. Kind regards.

cards.title: New Year Greetings
cards.inscription: Belmont Dec 28-12-09. Dear Cousin: I must send you a card to let you know how disappointed we were that we did not get down. Was going Friday but when we got up, could scarcely show our noses out with the Storm and then got all ready to go on Monday, when it was a worse storm than ever. So that was our luck. Pretty good don’t you think? The roads are blocked up something terrible here. Perhaps we will be able to get down some other time later on in the water. Hope you are all well and will have a very Happy New Year. Write soon.

cards.title: Two smiling women.
cards.inscription: East Baltic July 10th/09 Dear Friend, I seen you name in the PC Exchange. Would be more than glad to exchange with you. I am sorry I cannot send you a view just now but if you wish I will send you one later. Yours Lovingly, Joseph A. Campbell, East Baltic PEI Lot 46

cards.title: My Xmas Wish.
cards.inscription: Dec 23rd My dear friend, how I long to see you, and I want you to send me Ellens adress. I have never heard from her for oh so long. How is she. I have not been very well all ? and hope all are well with you? The Dummy was buried Tuesday. From Mary

cards.title: A pretty maid, whose gleeful smile, No affectation hides, nor guile.
cards.inscription: Dear Bernie, Have been expecting to hear from you for quite a while. Did you get the money for the spinning safely? Hope so. We brought home the yarn the Friday after you sent the parcel and mailed the money that day. You will likely have heard that we have our baby safe and sound. She came to us Sep 22, two weeks tomorrow. Bessie is to be one of her names. We have not settled on the others yet. Bernie dear, write soon, a card at least, telling us how you are. Best wishes to you all. Lovingly, Elsie. Oct 5/15. To Mrs. Neil N. McNevin, Milo, Lot 9, PEI

cards.title: Four sailboats at rest - photo.
cards.inscription: Dear Laura, How are you getting along? I am dreadfully lonesome tonight. I hardly know what to do with myself. Have to go away tomorrow for a few days. Don’t you pity me. Ain’t it awful to be a child. Lovingly yours, Bertie.

cards.title: For Memory’s Sake. Just a little greeting card I send to you today. And hopes that happiness and joy will light your pain away.
cards.inscription: Box 8 Alliston PEI Jan 3 15. Dear friend, how have you been this long time? Did you have a good time xmas? Have just finished writing a letter to Eloise. Do you two ever have any ? with the man on the hill and does he take ? with him?

cards.inscription: Aug 16th Dear Mother & Dad, Hope Mother’s health is fine and that your fingers are okay. Suppose the girls are home now. Mary is improving very much. We are having a fine holiday in this beautiful country.

cards.inscription: Hello Sadie and Geo, I’m still here, I am having a wonderful rest but a little lonesome for Rus. Expect to leav for home next Wednesday. How do you like the look of this Hotel? Will see you soon.

cards.inscription: Dear Mother, I now set down to let you know that I am smart hope that you are the same. I like the place. Did you hear from Stephen? Write soon. Send me his addresses.

cards.title: Prince of Wales College, Charlottetown, P.E.I.
cards.inscription: Dear Nita, I am so disappointed in not seeing you I have left a parcel at Merricks? with Mr L Bradley for you hope you will get it. Why couldn’t you meet me at the boat next Fri at 11 o’oclock as I leave for home this day. Florrie.

cards.inscription: Dear Friend, Received your very pretty postal some time ago and should have answered it before but hope you will pardon me for not doing so. You are missing all our big parties now. Do you attend many in Belmont? Send me another card soon and I shall be more prompt in answering it. When did you hear from Sarah E? Had a card from her a few days ago. From Jamie McPherson.

cards.title: Main St. Souris, P.E.I.
cards.inscription: 6-27-10 I live in the country, on a farm. This view of Souris I am sending is our nearest village which means seven miles from where I live. It is there we go to do our shopping. Of course we have small stores right around use. Lettie Bruce.

cards.title: Provincial Building and Law Court, Charlottetown, P.E.I.
cards.inscription: Arrived home after a fine trip last night; this is a nice place. Fine and cool here. Wish you could be here.

cards.inscription: Mother received Basil’s card today, and eager to tell you if you wish to stay over til Monday to do so. We would wish that you could be in two places at the one time, and since that cannot be, we will deny ourselves in someone else’s favour this time. Lillie wants you to get her 10 cents worth of Boracic Powder. Pam was disappointed as well as the rest. With love to all. Ada To Miss Florence Haslam, 210 Kent Street, Charlottetown, PEI.

cards.title: Souris West Bridge, P.E.I.
cards.inscription: Lloydminster May 4th. Dear Mother, I have arrived at last. Left Summerside Apr 15th got here May 3rd. I like this country fine. Tom. GS write soon.

cards.title: Alberton, P.E. Island.
cards.inscription: July 8, 13 Dear Sister, Being as you can’t get down, thought I would send you this card, let you see what it looks like here. Going to have a big time here Thursday. Going to a picnic tomorrow if pleasant but it looks very much like rain. Uncle John and Pa are having a great time. Pa is on the go all the time. We were down with Uncle Archie yesterday. Give my love to Willis and keep a good share for yourself. Lovingly, Fred.

cards.inscription: Dear friend, Many thanks for the pretty post cards that I received a long time ago and please excuse me for not writing sooner. So good bye from your post card friend.

cards.title: Evening Shadows, Summerside, Prince Edward Island
cards.inscription: Your postals arrived today but you gave us address, so are sending this to H. We leave here on 5:45 a.m. Saturday. I ? Friday and arrive at 26 Summer St. Sat morning. Have had such a good time and acquired such a color. We have beautiful drives and see lovely views. The coloring is so vivid here that things at home will sure look faded. Much to tell you when we meet. Tignish PEI Aug 25, 1908.

cards.inscription: Aug 18 1925: How are you Dorothy and little Joy, and Sonny? We have been staying here since the first of the month, and are enjoying our holiday very much, the bathing is ideal and we play golf down on the sand dunes. We also have “slack” golf up at the hotel and tennis, and so we are able to fill up every minute of the day. I expect we shall be leaving Saturday. Much love from Irene.

cards.inscription: July 28 1953 Thomas L Clairmont. We are having a nice rainy morning and as I have a good book I am quite pleased. This is the beach in front of the hotel and the swimming is simply wonderful. It was a ? trip down and we didn’t set in until after 1 o’clock on Saturday night. I hope you are not working too hard and that the weather is cooler.

There is much useful information in it. This is another poor print of one of my pictures. Bedeque, P.E.I. Dunk River in the distance. Papa.

cards.inscription: Dear Mrs. B, Just a line to let you know what we have been doing today. We went to the top of Yarmouth lighthouse and the view was grand. I stood the climb better than Pa. He was puffing like a steam engine when we reached the top. There is a war ship in the harbor now and I expect we shall visit it.

cards.inscription: Aug 20th. Am staying at this hotel on Prince Edward Island. Quite a place out in the Gulf of St. Lawrences and surrounded on 3 sides by water. Having a good rest, which is what the Dr. ordered. Ralph

cards.inscription: add Belle River, P.E.I. Dear Mrs. Verrill, Have not forgotten you. Hope you have all been well. I have been well and safely landed on P.E.I. Had a letter from Jennie. I have written to Mrs. Watson. Hope to hear from you soon. Kind regards to Mr. Verrill and wishing you and bring 1910. Your friend, Katie Mackintosh.

cards.inscription: Dec 24th Dear Friend, I am sending you this card as I have no Xmas one but this will do just as well. I am going to write you a letter. Write soon, Amy.

cards.inscription: Charlottetown, P.E.Is. Sat. Happy birthday from us, We will take care of you when we get home. It snowed some last night. It was rough coming the 14 mi from Nova Scotia to P.E.I. I was sea sick. Love Mother.

cards.inscription: Dear Family, A beautiful A.M. after a terrible rainy day. Went to a “shindig” last night and to mass yesterday. We are still on the go from AM to PM meeting all the rel. Don’t know if I’ll get any play. This is not the church we went to will get some snaps. Yesterday I got some films. Love to all.

cards.title: Pastoral Scene, P.E. Island.
cards.inscription: Ch’Town 7/27/14 Dearest Sis: Received your letter yesterday. I had just been scolding about you not writing. We were to Methodist church this morning. I think we will go to Baptist this evening. There is going to be baptism. Yours lovingly.

cards.inscription: Aug 6 - 29 Having a lovely time. Would like to stay longer. Waiting for our dinner now. Plenty of trout. See you soon.

cards.title: Central St., Summerside, P.E.I.
cards.inscription: Charlottetown PEI Canada Octo 18th 13. We are very well but the weather is not good. We spent the night in house in this street on this card. We went to see the Longworths off by boat & took Joan Longworth with us. We shall go that way when we leave the Island. Tell Mother to write to the Pryors. Hampstead now and not here anymore. We sail on the Canada on Nov 1st. Will send mother a word from Montreal. Love to all from Auntie Enid.

cards.title: Lumbering near Souris, P.E. Island (Photo Acorn)
cards.inscription: Charlottetown PE Island Jany 13. I hope you are having a nice winter & plenty of skating. We have not much snow yet, not enough for tobogganing and snowshoeing but the Indians say there will be plenty next month. Aunt E. loves sleigh driving. Love to all.

cards.title: Exhibition Building, P.E. Island.
cards.inscription: Dear Jane, I enjoyed my visit in Fredericton very much. I only wish I could have remained longer. The exhibition opened here today and we are having very disagreeable weather for it. James.

cards.inscription: How are you getting along in school? Lots of love to you and Whitcomb. Gramma

cards.inscription: Am having a great time here. It sure is some place. We are going to see a fox ranch this afternoon. One of the owners is coming in his car.

cards.inscription: Got a new tire in Bathurst N.B. Left about 9:30 A.M. Travelled leisurely to Cape Tormentine where we got ferry to Borden, P.E.I. This boat. Was interviewed by Rep of Gulf Broad. Co. Ltd. Got two letters of credit for $2.00 apiece.

cards.inscription: July 15, 27 Letter just rec’d. Also one of 8th. Mailed you a letter since card was sent. You may have left house before it was delivered. For some reason mail is 24 hours longer from Mabon Hill than from Boston.

cards.title: Winter Service between Mainland & Charlottetown, P.E.I.
cards.inscription: Dear May: A letter is coming some day. This is a fore runner. I enjoyed yours very much. Love, Blanche

cards.title: Provincial Building & Law Court, Charlottetown, P.E.I.
cards.inscription: {part of a longer letter} …at present and I like sewing fine. I have been here a month now. My aunt lives about 8 miles from my own home. You may expect me over any evening to see your large collection of cards. It has always been a great desire of mine to someday visit England Scotland and other countries over there and if ever I do I will call to see you sure. This is Thanksgiving day. Well I must close for now, hoping to hear from you soon again. Your Loving friend Ruby Brown

cards.inscription: Covehead Dec 13 1913 Dear Ryckman: Just to remind you of the Christmas season. With much love from Aunt Annie. To Master Ryckman Alexander, Lachute, Box 234, Quebec.

cards.title: Potatoes grow big here. At Charlottetown. Copyright Canada 1910 by Canadian Post Card Co., Toronto.
cards.inscription: Covehead Oct 9 1914. Do you grow potatoes as big as these? Write soon & tell me. All here are well. Hope you & Lassie and mother & father are well too. Love to all, Aunt Annie. Master Ryckman Alexander, Lachute, Quebec

cards.title: Trout Stream near Montague, P.E.I.
cards.inscription: 7/6/06 We have had a most interesting voyage. Have been rocked to sleep in our beds in the most vigorous manner. The floor is still rocking under my feet although we are on terra firma. Hope you are all well. Marshall & Elizabeth.

cards.title: Pleasant View Beach, Hampton, P.E.I.
cards.inscription: “Hello Tracadie” Did you get that cure for your cold yet? “Don’t forget the Harbour”. Yours, Peg. To Mr John J. McInnis, Tracadie Cross, P.E.I.

cards.inscription: P.E.I. is just as pretty as ever. Go in swimming every day. Everybody is fine. Mildred Brookes.

cards.inscription: Aug 24/51 Dear Mum, Having a grand time wish you were here. It’s really beautiful. How is wee Dave? Love…

cards.inscription: Ch’town Friday. Yours rec’d OK and you young mischief to raise my curiosity, and then not to tell me how has “been and gone and done it.” But cheer up, I’ll get even with you. Do wait till I get home before visiting O if it is possible, eh? We came back from Hampton last night. Great time there. Will write soon. Yours,

cards.title: Soldiers’ Monument, Charlottetown
cards.inscription: Dear friend, I received the papers. Many thanks for them. We are all well, hoping you are enjoying the same blessing. I wish you a happy new year.

cards.title: S. S. Prince Edward Island Leaving Tormentine for Borden, P.E.I.
cards.inscription: 8/3/25 As I am short of time and cards will you please tell the other folks I will see them later. Everything is going fine. Clarence

cards.inscription: Bob: The fishing is excellent - if you care to cut thru six feet of ice to get at it! I’m within 50 miles of my destination, but can’t go or come, because the roads are blocked. Okie O’Connor.

cards.inscription: As you will see I’m a long way from home. Came around the Gaspe pen. and intend to go to Halifax tomorrow. We are motoring and having a lovely trip. Hate to think of work soon again. Lilla C.

cards.inscription: Please pardon my delay in answering your cards. It was very pretty. Yes I am enjoying my vacation fine. Will try and get some local views to send you.

cards.title: Morrell River, Prince Edward Island
cards.inscription: Arrived home safe had a delightful trip will write you later.

cards.inscription: Summerside PEI 10th Sept 1892 Dear Sirs, Please send me a pamphlet of your comptometer & oblige. A.D. Caldwell.

cards.title: West River, P.E. Island
cards.inscription: Aug 3/1914. Dear Bessie: I suppose you are still at home working hard since your mother went away. We are having a good time here and it is grand and cool. I hate to go home. I suppose Jennie is having a good time also. Will see you I suppose at the next meeting. Goodbye for now from yours truly, Mabel E McClure

cards.title: Coming through one of the delightful driveways at the Entrance to Beach Grove Inn, Prince Edward Island.
cards.inscription: Dear Ma: This is a beautiful place on Prince Edward’s Island. The birches and evergreens are like Maine. Bidon.

cards.title: Bishop’s Palace and R.C. Cathedral Charlottetown
cards.inscription: July 2 1912 Chtown PEI Dear Mrs B, We are boarding just opposite to this church. I wis ou could see the way the people attend it. I came over on Friday will be home Wednesday. I will write to you both as soon as I can. Lovingly,

cards.title: Prince County Hospital, Summerside, P.E. Island
cards.inscription: Dear Wilfred, Just a few lines to congratulate you on your coming birthday, Mar 3rd. I hope you are well & busy curling as usuel. Love Lizzie.

cards.title: Queen Square Gardens, Charlottetown, P.E.I.
cards.inscription: Dear Gertie, How are you. Hope your well. Mother & Wilf are not going home till Monday so she says take care of everything. Drop her a card and tell her how you are getting long. Love Lizzie.

cards.title: Government Fish Drier Souris, Prince Edward Island
cards.inscription: Oct 8th, Dear Bess, Hope you are enjoying ? as usual guess I will call around and … ?

cards.title: Water Street, looking West, Summerside, P.E.I.
cards.inscription: Frend Dudley. I have returned from P.E. Island and will remain here a few days and then for Boston. I had a great trip to Nova Scotia. I hope you are well and getting on fine. I am well and am having a fairly good time.

cards.title: Maint St. Souris, P.E. Island (looking west)
Armouries & West Kent School, Charlottetown, P.E.I.
cards.inscription: Tuesday evening. Dear Mother, Received Mary’s letter. Glad that you arrived there safe and are all well. Alex’s finger is much better now. I will write to Mary in a few days, am in a hurry tonight. Will mai this on train in the morning.

cards.title: Shaw’s Hotel Brackley Beach, P.E. Island
cards.inscription: Hope you are having a lovely holiday. No motors are allowed on Prince Edward Island. It is a beautiful farming country and quiet too. The air is so refreshing. Arthur Parks.

cards.title: Kildare Capes, P.E.I.
cards.inscription: Dear Hazel, Well here I am on Pig Island and it sure is a grand place. Wish you could see the scenery. Went digging clams today. The sands on the shores is white as milk. Wish you were here to go swimming with me. Going home Sat. Love Margaret.

cards.title: Won’t you drop a line to a poor lonely soul in Summerside
cards.inscription: Summerside PEI Box 371. Dear Friend - Just a card to let you know we are alive. Capt & I are busy collecting. We were away four days last week and are going away to the country this week. I hope you are doing well with your collecting. Kind regards to all. From M Burton, Lieut.

cards.title: RPPC of Seaside Hotel, Cape Tormentine, N.B.
cards.inscription: Dear Friend, Rec’d Gorda’s postal and was sorry that we missed seeing you but hope you will come down here and see us some time soon. If I am not too late let me congratulate you. You are an exceedingly lucky fellow. So also is Gorda. Will tell you more about it when I see you. Yours Very Truly, B.J. Seaman

cards.title: RPPC of Montague Bridge
cards.inscription: Do you recognize this? Montague Bridge, Aug 20/09. Minnie, Mrs. R and myself were down to Geo Town yesterday; went down on train came back on boat. Had a nice time.

cards.title: D.G.S. Minto Icebound, Winter Service Pictou N.S. to Georgetown P.E.I.

cards.title: All Souls Chapel, St. Peter’s Cathedral, Charlottetown, P.E. Island
cards.inscription: This little chapel which will hold only 40 people was built in memory of a much loved Bishop, the work all being done by PEI workmen. The memorial paintings are by Robert Harris, Canada’s most famous artist who was once a choir boy in this church and went to Italy later to study art. The face of his mother is embodied in the picture which shone on the right, a very noble face and under it the inscription “Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you.” Other pictures are “Christ blessing little children”, “The stoning of Stephen”, “Christ walking on the water”, “the Raising of Dorcas”. There are also very fine stained glass windows, tho small.

My hands and feet more a little cold when I got there. Wm Houston & wife were here when I got here, expect to go up to grandma’s tomorrow (Sat) - please send down that tray cloth as soon as you can. Folks are all quite well. The roads were real good except a few slews on the hillsides. Going to Mr. Bulman’s tonight. Did not leave S.Side til after 3 o’clock. They expected me to go right up to grandma’s. I feel somewhat tired. Love to all, Annie.

cards.inscription: From Harry Holman: These two pics are taken from the east side of Prince Street. One is from a spot just south of the corner with Kent Street looking south. The other is just south of the corner with Grafton St. Looking north. The "grassy knoll" in the military parade photo is the NE corner of St. Paul's church grounds. The church tower and the distinctive shape of the eve of the Sunday School building can be faintly seen on the photo facing south. None of the buildings on the view facing north have survived. The corner building was replaced by Zion Presbyterian church about 1911. The three story brick building on the north view was a grocery story on the corner of Prince and Kent. I attach a copy of an insurance atlas image ca. 1903 showing this block. The houses are the same in both photos. It is interesting that the views show the parade both coming and going (if they are the same parade, which is questionable). The military parade route is east on Grafton and then south on Prince. The fraternal order parade is heading north on Prince Street. They are both at the same time of the year so it could be the same event. Unlikely to be the opening or closing of the legislature as the fraternal bodies did not participate. Lots of other parades however during Jubilee celebrations, Boer war events and coronations. See also 3178

Leo finished a book of ph0tos for me, the best I ever saw. To Miss Florence Haslam Stone Cottage Springfield PE Island

cards.inscription: Sept 11/53 Hi Mr B. I expect you have heard ? this that I am if all goes well, spending the winter with Lloyd’s family. Does that surprise you? Geo. returned by plane this a.m. We were up at 4:30 am. Painters are here and we started threshing today so are very busy. D&R got Gracie’s interesting letter Aunt M. came out of the hos. last Sat. Love to all, M. To Mr. B.P. Colclough, Box 250, Newmarket, Ontario.

cards.inscription: Monday. My dear: Here we are at our little “Island Home” once again and it is so quiet and lovely here. How I wish you were with us. Ruth would enjoy this view and the people here as everyone has a good story to tell. You are consistently in our thoughts and we do hope everything is going well with our beloved church and church school. We miss you all. The weather is perfect. Blueberries are not plentiful this year. Hope your brother is feeling better. Affectionate greetings to each and all.

cards.inscription: July 25, 1907 Received your letter this morning. Also the card signed AOP. Wait until I get hold of Mabel! I was to a tea party at Murray Harbor yesterday. I would write a letter but Stephen wants me to hurry. He is just the same old boy. We may possibly go home on Friday, as the boat gets into Pictou at half-past three. If we do not go I shall write again.

cards.inscription: Ct’town PEI 8/25/04 Dear Fannie, Your letter rec’d. Glad to hear from you. We are about dead today. We were invited to accompany the superintendant of the Railroad on his first inspection of the new branch. We had a delightful day. Tonight we took a carriage to make a few calls. Made 12, Not bad for one night. We leave here tomorrow at 1PM for home. Love to all, Florence and Fred.

cards.inscription: Charlottetown, Prince Edward Island July 20/15 Dear Ernest, Here is a card for your collection, written way up in Canada where I am attending the Sons of Temperance National Convention. That reminds me that I received 5.00 from Norwich all or part of what money the Good Templar Lodge had left when they gave up its charter. I put it into 50 copies of the National Monthly. I have been trying to think and now it has just come, the name A.A. Baldwin, who sent it. Kind regards to Mrs. Smith, Betty and yourself.

Say, I’ve a lot more time now if I come home Saturday, since the trained changed. May come before long. I have half an idea of walking home some Friday when the roads dry up. They seem to have sent that atlas to me so I am sending it right along to you. Look - send me a nice card. They don’t cost any more. David. PS Did you get Spalding’s catalogue? There are only 2 footballs we might get in it. $1.50 and $2.25. I guess we will get the $1.50 one.

cards.inscription: It is so windy today the fisherman can’t go out to fish, so the men of this household are digging clams for future bait. There is a flock of geese in the daisy field outside my window and I think I never again will speak disrespectfully of a goose. They are noble-looking animals that require no feeding. I know not what of wind and wave and nausea lies between me and Cambridge, but I shall always be glad I came to this lovely spot. Mrs. K stops in her work every now and then to ask after this one and that one, Ian and Jane included. Aunt Etta.

cards.inscription: Central Bedeque Sep 11th Dear friend, Have thought of you so often since I came home and the good time we all had the time you took us to the lake. I think of you all every day and wish I could drop in again. Ivan is fine altho he seemed a little tired when he came home. Am sending you a fox picture but my son is taking some real ones so if good will send you one. Hope the Dr. has had no more broken bones to set. Love E Dawson

From Your True Friend, Ivey L.

cards.inscription: Tues Aug 13 1918, Mrs. C and I came here on 10.15 a.m. train expecting to go back at 1.15. Mrs Brown wouldn’t hear of it - we are having a fine time. Been out walking. She is full of fun as ever. …{lengthy}

cards.inscription: We are now back in New Brunswick at Gt. George, with Ruth Russell’s cousins, and having a delightful time. Tomorrow we go on the Alice Fowler at Boothbay Harbor, Maine, then to Clarissa in Arlington, Mass. I wish I could send a supply of the fresh cool breeze from the Bay of Fundy to you. Love, Bud.

cards.inscription: Sep 28 1945 Hello Dora How are you all. I am down here at present. Gordon is working here…{lengthy}… It is quite cool here. Began to feel like fall the year. Am thinking about taking a trip on this boat today if Gordon can get away. Want to go across the P.E.I. it is 9 miles across from here in this boat. It takes the trains right on takes 12 freight or passenger cars, and auto as well. Bye bye.

cards.inscription: Ch Town 8/2/03 Dear Friend jo, This is Sunday noon. I have just come in from church. I always enjoy the music here as it is usually a little nicer than listening to myself in the choir in Annapolis. I am enjoying the summer very much. The Island is beautiful. This city particularly. This is a view near the park and very nice here, a great resort in the evenings. I have been here 2 weeks here 2 weeks longer then I go to Souris & Georgetown & Montague. i have a fellow working for me in the western end of the Isle & I get a boy to help me deliver for me in the city. I would be pleased to have ?? F.P. Freeman

cards.inscription: Charlottetown P.E.I. 16 Aug 25. Dear Arthur, this tree reminds me of the historic one on the cliff at Leland - except that lambs are taking your place. We are fortunate to have sparkling weather. Must plan to come here the next time you come home. Affectionately, Mary.

cards.inscription: I am quite well. Letter follows at first opportunity. Gillis M. June 30th 16. To Mrs. Wm Gillis, Orwell Cove P.O., P.E.Island, Canada.

cards.title: Montague Bridge, Prince Edward Island, Canada.
cards.inscription: Dear Bill, Have been all over P.E.I. today. It is 145 miles long - 34 wide - are leaving on the ferry in the morning. Isn’t much to see, some lovely views and beautiful farms and farm bldgs, Love, Mother

cards.inscription: I did not get a chance to see you before I started. I had a very nice trip down on the boat and it is lovely down here. Will send you a card soon again.

cards.inscription: Nov 11. 14. Just to let you know I arrived all right last night. A fine trip only on boat, it was awful rough, came near feeding the fish, am going to Summerside some time this week for a short time, then back here later. Will write you later and give you my address.

cards.title: Morell Bridge, P.E.I.
cards.inscription: Dear Florence, I have just received your card and hope you will have a lovely time and a very nice rest. You must have been very tired. I suppose your mother has gone to Hampton.

cards.inscription: Dear Cousin G., Received your P.C. five days ago. Was glad to hear that you had such a good time. Olive is in going to C.B.G. She didn’t get the chance to run after me. I dodge her every time. We have nine boarders. Not much work (ahem). I was sick last week as it was pretty hard on … Cousin Arthur is back with the old girl again and Nick Heartz is in going to college again. Done writing as card is hard to write on. Write Soon, love from all.

cards.inscription: This is the nearest village & railroad station to where we are. Will try and write a letter today. Aubrey.

cards.inscription: I am having a delightful time. Maude.

cards.title: Queen Street, Charlottetown, P.E.I.

cards.inscription: Dear ??, Your letter arrived yesterday. Blanch and May today. Mary has just been trying to bribe me to take her to the store, she said “If you will come Aunt Louise I’ll get you an orange and tell you all about Daddy. Will write later. Do you see old Perry anywhere on other side?

cards.title: Queen Street, Charlottetown, P.E.I.
cards.inscription: Sep 29 PEI My dear Edna, This is a lovely day and and we are having a lovely time. We’ve been around town this morning. It is a lovely place. We had a nice time on the boat and were not too sick.

cards.inscription: Dec 6/11 Here I am in Hillview spending a very pleasant time with my Uncle & Aunt in their new home, sorry you cannot be with me. I expect to get home Sunday if weather keeps fine. Yours, Margaret. I suppose by this time you would need this boat to cross the river.

cards.title: Mushroom Rock, Prince Edward Island
cards.inscription: You will see by this I am on my vacation and having a good rest. Will write you when I get back. I hope you are well. Much love.

cards.title: Public Buildings, Charlottetown, P.E.I.
cards.inscription: Tuesday PM Dear Laura, Arrived in Charlottetown Saturday night and came to Souris today. We will go to Cardigan and Georgetown this week, and then go to the other end of the Island. Expect to spend next Sunday in Summerside. Have to get up most awful early to catch trains. Tomorrow it leaves at 6:30 am. It must be lovely here in summer.

cards.inscription: Aug 2, 1929 Yesterday morning during a four hour ferry trip we made acquaintance of some people who had a fox ranch - visited the place later in the day and enjoyed very much looking around. Ella.

cards.inscription: “kirk” on front. May 19/09 Dear Jim - Rec’d your card today. You will be surprised to get word back from me so soon as I am such a poor hand at writing. I was up to Carter’s bookstore today and saw this card, thought it would send it to you. This is where I am most of the time after working hours. Getting along pretty well doo. Yours, Fred.

cards.inscription: 11/2/10 Just a card to let you know we are still living and often think of you. We intended to have seen you long before this but we have been kept going some, lately. Will try to run out some time next week. Will let you know when. If you are down town drop in to see us. Best regards to ? and yourself, from all and yours as ever, Kittie {see also 3910}

cards.title: View of Murray Harbor, P.E.I.
cards.inscription: Dear Maryann, Here is the card I promised to send you from home. Marissa is beside me has been off riding with me all day and now wants to go home. With love.

cards.title: Harbor, Tignish, P.E.I.
cards.inscription: Well here goes for the Prince’s Island. Anybody here got a match? No? Too bad. Well, there are still some more cards you will be getting from round the world. I see 3 men and a boat, another boats. Life is just like this everywhere. I’ll give you this card free if you can tell me what this stuff is they intend to put off. “No good thing will he withhold from them who walk uprightly.” We all must walk that way.

cards.inscription: Dear Dolley, You will see by this that I have not gone away yet. Are not going until Sept. first. I am visiting my aunts home. Will be up here some time. This is the place where they own black foxes. They are having great luck this year.

cards.title: RPPC of Kildare River
cards.inscription: Dear Cora, Thanks very much for the gloves and fan, they arrived safely yesterday morning. This is a picture of Kildare River, taken from the side of a hill. The river is really way below in a valley, although the picture makes it look on a level. We will see you in a few weeks now, n’est-ce pas? Lillian

cards.inscription: Sept 23 - Dearest John, Isn’t this a queer rock. And this place is very pretty but such slippery roads makes us nervous. Suppose you are working hard at school. How do you like it? I see you have to do your studying at night. After a while, you will find it easier as you get used to new work and teachers. Be patient. Dear mother has to work hard. Heaps of love from Norma

cards.title: Summerside Harbour
cards.inscription: Thurs 23 - Dearest Ruth, I was so glad to get a letter from you and Grace. I was ready to start home the mail is so slow in this part of the country. Prince Edward Island does not appeal to me with its slippery roads. We start back on steamer tomorrow on to Halifax St John and on to ?? Send letter there it is late so must go to bed. Heaps of love to all from Mother. {see 3933}

cards.inscription: Dear John, This is near Gowan's Brae where Daddy's {indistinct} used to live. We fished along the edge and they say there are lots of trout and perch in the spring. We didn't catch a fish there but got a few bites. {continues}

I have quite recovered and have great reasons to be thankful as I was quite ill. We are settled for the winter at Mrs. McKechnie’s, where Maggie and Helen were entertained, but I expect to go up to Moncton before long to get some of my things.

cards.title: Canada Post Card
cards.inscription:
You must excuse the formality and haste of this note — pressure of time.
Dear Mrs. S.,
The petitions came in this morning, and not a word yet on the other. I sent you my copy, and if I do not hear by Monday evening I will send you the original copy.
The petitions in question are in the hands of my sister here, so you will only have to send the other two, and your work as far as they are concerned will be complete; but — could are you not willing to call upon Dr. Dennis, trustee of Parliament — either from a hearing in the legislature, or from Mrs. Archibald? We have done so for this country, and if you would care for a copy of the letter we send, I would send it at your request.
I am writing in confidence, as the matter is delicate and should not be spoken of openly.
I would help you, but I don’t promise that I can do better. By the way, some new things are coming about. The C.P.R. Co., as I mention in [illeg.], seems we were earlier than before. Geo. Baird would say we must not allow matters to rest when work can still be done.
I rely upon your discretion in this matter, as before.
Yours, S.

I live at No. 53 Fox Avenue, Rosebank Fur Farms. I am daily visited by men and women of high station and those versed in animal lore especially my own silver fox bunch. They all agree that I am a thoroughbred and the image of my distinguished ancestor named above. I am petted by my master, well cared for by my keeper in fact have every reason to enjoy my existence here in my beautiful wooded home. I have many companions much like myself, many of them like me are of the Dalton fox blood royal."

cards.title: RPPC of Alma Cottage Farm and family
cards.inscription: Alma Cottage. The barn is where the house should be (on front). Dear Aunt Ellen, We thought we would run up to Lowell to see you as here we are house barn windmill and the family. Suppose Uncle Cyru is having a big time. Tell him we sent word to Henry that he was on his way after the cigars. Mama and Papa had baby in town today to get his picture taken…\nDESCRIPTION OF HISTORIC PLACE 38-40 Upper Prince Street, or Alma Cottage as it was once known, is a wood framed, Georgian inspired former residence of the Haviland family. Located on a treed lot, the house was one of the first in the area and included a much larger lot until the Haviland family subdivided the property. Once called Haviland Lane because of its association with the prominent family, the name of the street was later changed to Upper Prince Street. The designation encompasses the building's exterior and parcel; it does not include the building's interior. HERITAGE VALUE The heritage value of 38-40 Upper Prince Street lies in its association with the Haviland family and its role in supporting the streetscape. Alma Cottage was constructed in the 1840s. It is not clear if Thomas Heath Haviland (1822-1895) built the structure, but he and his family were residents of the home until almost the middle of the Twentieth Century. Thomas Heath Haviland was born into one of Charlottetown's most prominent and influential families. His father, Thomas Heath Haviland senior (c. 1795-1867), was a lawyer, office-holder, land agent/proprietor, banker and politician. The junior Haviland would follow his father's example and become an active member of Charlottetown society. Thomas Heath Haviland was educated in Belgium and returned to Prince Edward Island in the early 1840s, where he studied law. In 1846, he was both called to the Bar, and elected to the House of Assembly. Haviland served in a number of roles during his political career including Colonial Secretary, Member of the Executive Council, Solicitor-General, Provincial Secretary, Leader of the Opposition and Speaker of the House of Assembly. A strong advocate for Confederation, he was an active participant at the Quebec Conference in 1864 and later in the final negotiations for PEI's terms of union with the Dominion of Canada in 1873. He was called to the Senate by Sir John A. Macdonald on 18 October 1873 where he remained until he resigned in July 1879 to become the Lieutenant Governor of Prince Edward Island. Following his five year term in the Vice Regal office, he took over as Mayor of Charlottetown after the death of Henry Beer in 1886. He would serve in this role until 1893. Two of his major accomplishments while in office included the completion of the current Charlottetown City Hall building and the construction of a public water system. Not only a politician and officeholder, Haviland was also involved in business, the militia, the mental health facility, and Prince of Wales College. Thomas Heath Haviland and his wife, Anne Elizabeth Grubbe (1818-1902), who was also a member of the local elite, lived at Alma Cottage for many years. Their daughters, Edith Constance Haviland Peake (1847-1931), Eleanor Blanche Haviland (1858-1942) and son, barrister, Eustace Heath Haviland (1849-1932) lived at the home well into the Twentieth Century. For a time, Eleanor Blanche Haviland was the lone surviving member of the family until she died in 1942. Almost one year later, an auction notice appeared in the 27 August 1943 edition of the local newspaper, the Guardian that advertised the auction sale of the residence, land and personal effects of Eleanor Blanche Haviland. Alma Cottage was converted into an apartment building at some point in its history and remains in this role today. It has been suggested that the large addition on the back of the property was at one time the stable house. A large former home associated with a number of prominent residents, Alma Cottage helps support the Upper Prince Street streetscape. Sources: Heritage Office, City of Charlottetown Planning Department, PO Box 98, Charlottetown, PE C1A 7K2 #0006a CHARACTER-DEFINING ELEMENTS The following character-defining elements contribute to the heritage value of 38-40 Upper Prince Street: - The overall rectangular massing of the building - The wood shingle exterior - The mouldings painted in a contrasting colour, particularly the door and window surrounds - The gable roof with little eave overhang - The size and placement of the sash windows, including the grouped windows of the facade and the grouped windows of the porch - The style and centre placement of the door with a gable projection above - The size, placement and shape of the porches located on the south side of the home - The large extension on the back of the home that may have once been the stable\nOther character-defining elements include: - The mature trees on the property - The location of the building on Upper Prince Street and its physical and visual relationship to its streetscape

cards.title: {rppc of the crew of the Village Belle, RNWM Police schooner}
cards.inscription: Souris PEI 8/8/14 We pulled in here for repairs to engine. Just leaving for BL {Baker Lake}. Hope we have got rid of the hoodoo. Kind Regards to all. WJB. “Hope we have got rid of the hoodoo.” — Souris, August 1914\nEngine trouble brought the Village Belle and an Arctic police expedition to Matthew McLean’s wharf at Souris. On 8 August 1914, Inspector Walter James Beyts sent this real photo postcard to R. S. Knight, care of the Royal North-West Mounted Police in Regina. “We pulled in here for repairs to engine, just leaving for B.L.,” he wrote, referring to Baker Lake. “Hope we have got rid of the hoodoo.”\nBeyts was heading north to investigate the deaths of travellers Harry Radford and George Street at Bathurst Inlet. The expedition encountered years of delays, and Inspector French replaced Beyts in 1916. The subsequent inquiry heard that Radford had attacked an Inuit guide who refused to leave his injured wife; it concluded that the killings had followed “great provocation,” and no prosecution followed. This postcard preserves an unplanned Island stop in that much longer journey, with its commander still hoping the bad luck was behind him.

cards.inscription: To Mr. H.R. Stewart, 216 Peel St., Montreal. Sunday Aug 31/12. Dear Ron, I got your cards & the ?? of Ottawa, thank you very much. The tea yesterday was not too bad. It wasn’t nearly as bad as the thought of it was. I took this picture and printed it so you know what it is not very good. I saw Jennf on Friday, just passed him on the street. I was awfully lazy today, didn’t get up til three o’clock. I wasn’t feeling very well. Tob? is fine now. You must of had an awfully nice time in Ottawa, especially canoeing. School starts Tuesday, horrible thought. Beth comes in on Wednesday. Hope you will have a good time in Montreal. Good-by MLW.

Ceres first-class cakes and rusks: the finest.\nThe interesting discovery is that Ceres really did use collectible pictures to advertise its products. The Dutch Archive of Picture Albums documents several promotional series issued by the company, including Door Nederland (Through the Netherlands), a collection of 120 numbered views dating to approximately 1901–1908. Ceres even sold a small album for collecting them.

cards.inscription: Georgetown PEI, October 21st 1914 Dear loving S.H. I thought that I would drop you a card to let you know that we got here safe. We had it fine coming over. We got here the 19th. This is a fine little town. Today is Sunday and I feel awful lonesome. I didn’t go ashore yet. I wish I was with you tonight to pass away the evening … {erased} … don’t you think so. Don’t you let no one see this card. I don’t know if we are going to stay here or not.

cards.inscription: Montague PEI July 13, 1923 Dear Forrest, We have been down here for nearly three weeks now. Mother was sick when we arrived and has been sick ever since, so she is not enjoying her holiday very much. However she is better now. It is lovely here right by the ocean. When are you having your holidays and what are you going to do with them? Hope you will be able to run down to Lennoxville in the fall. Love to you both, Alina.
